observations.attempt: Traced the cost of a single inbound WS frame on the new chat-subscribe path and searched the gateway for any per-connection rate limit, debounce, or in-flight-request cap on it. Found none: every `{type:'subscribe', channel:'chat', conversationId}` frame -- including a REPEAT subscribe to a conversation the connection already holds, and a subscribe to a conversation the caller does not own -- unconditionally triggers one full awaited round trip through deps.authorizeChatSubscription (an HTTP POST to Core's /internal/realtime/chat-authorization plus one scoped Postgres query in realtimeChatService's store.getConversation) BEFORE the isNew/already-subscribed check is ever consulted. Each inbound `socket.on('message', ...)` frame is also dispatched as its own independent `void (async () => {...})()` with no queueing, so a burst of frames on one connection fires that many authorization round trips concurrently, unbounded.
evidence: services/gateway/src/ws/connection.ts:164-198 -- handleChatSubscribe calls `await deps.authorizeChatSubscription(conn, conversationId)` unconditionally as its first substantive step, and only AFTER that resolves does it check `isNew = !conn.chatSubscriptions.has(conversationId)` -- so a duplicate subscribe to an already-held, legitimately-owned conversation still pays the full Core+Postgres round trip every time, not just the first time.

services/gateway/src/ws/connection.ts:285-327 -- the socket 'message' handler wraps each frame's processing in its own `void (async () => {...})()` with no per-connection queue, semaphore, or rate limiter; N frames in flight on one connection produce up to N concurrent handleChatSubscribe/authorizeChatSubscription calls.

grep -rniE 'rate.?limit|throttle|maxPayload|debounce' services/gateway/src (excluding tests) -- zero matches anywhere in the gateway; no bound exists at any layer between an inbound WS frame and an outbound Core HTTP call.

This is a genuinely new amplification path introduced by CH-05: the pre-existing repo-scoped `handleSubscribe` (ws/connection.ts:115-125) is fully synchronous and makes zero network calls at subscribe time, so it could not be abused the same way; CH-05's chat-subscribe path is the first WS-inbound frame type in this codebase whose handling is gated on an awaited Core round trip on every occurrence, including repeats.

finding.remediation_reference: Add a per-connection rate limit / in-flight-request cap on chat subscribe frames (and ideally on inbound WS message processing generally) before EACH one is allowed to trigger a fresh authorizeChatSubscription round trip -- e.g. a short-lived per-(connectionId, conversationId) memo bounded to the in-flight acquire (already partially exists via the isNew/acquire ordering, but only for the Redis-acquire side, not the authorization-call side), or a per-connection token bucket on inbound message processing overall. Not a tenant-isolation or RBAC-boundary failure (no cross-org/cross-user data is ever exposed by this path) and does not require a fix before merge, but should be tracked as a fast-follow given it is reachable by any single authenticated connection with no additional privilege.
